message.content: {"action": "ask_researcher", "args": {"question": "In the rate law dS/dt = -Vmax*S/(Km*(1 + I/KI) + S), does the symbol I denote (a) the free inhibitor state (constant at I(0)=2.0), or (b) the total inhibitor (free plus sequestered in the enzyme-inhibitor complex, which would grow as S is consumed)? The material presents both readings as equally authoritative and does not specify which one the rate expression uses."}, "reason": "The source explicitly presents two conflicting readings of I in the rate law and does not resolve which is intended; I must not choose."}
